key_insight: PEA spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites, slowing degradation under ambient light and thermal stress compared with BA spacers.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection is a stability-design lever for perovskite devices, but should be combined with surface passivation and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 perovskites under ambient light and thermal stress.
Used confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to assess degradation.
Examined morphology, lattice defects and luminescence in freshly exfoliated nanoflakes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparable initial room-temperature luminescence but slower degradation for PEA2PbI4, with both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI2 and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative lifetime or device-efficiency results, so improved material stability does not establish long-term solar-cell performance.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
